quizTarget: Replace b’s new Counter() with a. What prints?

essentialSupport.fact: A class defines fields and methods; new Counter() creates an instance. Each instance has its own non-static value field. A method call through a reference operates on that referenced object.
Counter b = new Counter() creates a second object. Counter b = a instead copies the reference: both variables then refer to the same object. It does not clone the fields.

The package-private Counter can share this Main.java file; only Main is public. With no written constructor, this class gets a default no-argument constructor. value starts at the explicitly supplied 0.

reasoning: Both references now designate the same object, so b.increment changes the value also observed through a.

quizTarget: Change new Session(12) to new Session(). What happens?

essentialSupport.fact: A constructor has the class name and no return type. new Session(12) passes 12 into that constructor. this refers to the object being initialized.
In this.minutes = minutes, this.minutes names the field and the bare minutes names the parameter. Assigning the parameter to itself would not initialize the field as intended.
Once this class declares Session(int), Java does not also generate a no-argument constructor. A new Session() call therefore needs a separately declared matching constructor.

reasoning: Only Session(int) is declared. Java does not synthesize the default no-argument constructor when another constructor is written.

quizTarget: Change the second request from 7 to 3. What does the final get return?

essentialSupport.fact: An invariant is a rule that valid objects maintain. This Level always stores a number from 0 through 3. Keeping value private prevents unrelated caller code from assigning an invalid number directly.
set returns false for an invalid next value and leaves the old field unchanged. Its public method provides a checked operation; get observes the current value without exposing a writable field.
Encapsulation helps enforce this class’s rule. It does not automatically validate every external input or make a class thread-safe.

reasoning: 3 satisfies the invariant, so the second call succeeds and stores 3.

quizTarget: Replace the element assignment with scores = new int[]{9}. What happens?

essentialSupport.fact: A static field belongs to the class rather than each instance. Ticket.issued counts constructor calls in this single-threaded example. Each Ticket still has its own final number assigned once by its constructor.

A final variable cannot be reassigned after initialization. If it holds an object or array reference, the referenced contents may still be mutable. final int[] scores fixes the array reference, not every array element.
static controls whether a field is class-wide; final controls assignment to the variable. Neither alone is a synchronization policy for concurrent mutation.

reasoning: Mutating an element was permitted, but replacing the reference stored in final scores is a different, forbidden assignment.

quizTarget: Create an Animal instead of a Cat but keep the same variable and call. What prints?

essentialSupport.fact: class Cat extends Animal inherits from Animal and provides its own implementation of sound(). A variable typed Animal may refer to a Cat object.

@Override asks the compiler to check that a method really overrides an inherited declaration. The matching name and parameter list matter; accidentally adding a parameter would create a different overload.
Calling the overridden instance method uses the actual object type at runtime. This rule is not a claim that fields or static methods have the same dynamic dispatch behavior.

reasoning: This Animal object uses Animal.sound. The reference’s declared type alone did not choose the Cat implementation.

quizTarget: Replace new Square() with new Shape(). What happens?

essentialSupport.fact: An abstract class may contain abstract methods without bodies. Shape.area() defines a required operation; the concrete Square supplies it.

A Shape reference can refer to a Square. You cannot instantiate Shape itself while it is abstract. Abstract classes can also contain fields, constructors and implemented methods; abstract does not mean every member lacks a body.

reasoning: An abstract type may be used for a reference, but it cannot be directly instantiated.

quizTarget: Remove public from ConsoleReporter.report(). Does the interface contract still compile?

essentialSupport.fact: An interface can describe behavior implemented by otherwise unrelated classes. This Reporter interface has one public abstract report() method; these modifiers are implicit on this declaration.
ConsoleReporter implements Reporter and defines public String report(). The implementation must not reduce the interface method’s public access. @Override checks the match.
The compiler checks method signatures, not whether returned text is truthful or useful. Interfaces can also have default or static methods, but this example needs only the abstract contract.

reasoning: The method required by the interface is public. A package-access implementation cannot satisfy that public contract.

quizTarget: Change the constructor’s minutes argument to 15. What prints?

essentialSupport.fact: record Session(String topic, int minutes) declares components and supplies a canonical constructor, accessors named topic() and minutes(), and component-based equals/hashCode/toString behavior.

Record component fields are final and the record class is final. A record is only shallowly immutable: a component referring to a mutable list can still observe list mutation unless you arrange defensive copying.
The String and int components used here do not expose a mutable list. The accessors are methods, not public fields; session.minutes() reads the component.

reasoning: Final components prevent later reassignment; they do not force every new instance to have identical component values.

quizTarget: Add final class Other implements Outcome without changing permits. What happens?

essentialSupport.fact: A sealed interface specifies permitted direct subtypes. Outcome permits only Success and Failure here. Those final classes cannot be subclassed further.

A permitted ordinary class must choose final, sealed, or non-sealed as required by the sealed hierarchy rules. non-sealed deliberately reopens that branch; sealed does not mean the objects are immutable.
An unrelated class cannot simply implement Outcome unless it is permitted. These top-level declarations share the same source file and unnamed package, satisfying the location rule for this example.

reasoning: The explicit permits clause limits direct implementations to Success and Failure.

quizTarget: Change mode to Mode.REST. Which switch result is printed?

essentialSupport.fact: An enum defines named instances of its own type. Mode.READ and Mode.REST are values of Mode, not arbitrary strings. == can compare enum identity directly.
The switch expression lists every constant, so no default branch is needed for this enum. Its arms return the String value assigned to action.

ordinal is a position, not a stable business identifier. If saving an enum choice outside a process, use a deliberate representation and handle unknown values rather than assuming declaration order never changes.

reasoning: The REST arm explicitly yields pause. Enum identity selects the arm; the result is the arm’s expression.

quizTarget: Give b the id 8. What changes in equals and the set size?

essentialSupport.fact: == compares reference identity for objects. equals can define logical equality. A record’s generated equals compares corresponding components, so two separate Key(7) instances are equal.

If equals returns true, the two objects must have the same hashCode. Unequal objects may still collide; a hash code is not a unique identifier. Records generate compatible equals and hashCode implementations.
HashSet uses hashing and equality to detect duplicates. Do not change fields that participate in equality while an object is a hash-based key; this record’s primitive component is stable.

reasoning: Different id components make the records unequal. Both distinct logical keys remain in the set; this does not require unique hashes for all possible records.

quizTarget: Keep Box<String> but pass 123 to new Box<>. What happens?

essentialSupport.fact: Box<T> uses T as a type parameter. Box<String> allows String values without asking callers to cast get(). Angle brackets describe compile-time type arguments.
The constructor, field and return type all use T. The diamond <> on new Box<> lets the compiler infer a suitable argument from the declaration and constructor call.

Java generics use reference types, not primitive arguments such as Box<int>. Wrapper types such as Integer can represent primitive values; boxing is explored shortly. Avoid raw Box declarations that discard useful generic checking.

reasoning: The target requires String while the int argument boxes to Integer. Generic inference does not invent a String conversion.

quizTarget: Replace Integer.valueOf(3) with the String "3". What happens?

essentialSupport.fact: <T extends Number> limits T to Number or one of its subtypes. The bound lets the method call Number.doubleValue without guessing whether every Object supports it.
In static <T extends Number> double asDouble(T value), the type-parameter declaration comes before the return type. This is a generic method, not a generic Main class.
Number includes wrapper types such as Integer and Double; String is not a Number. The bound permits a conversion method, not arbitrary operator arithmetic on T and not protection from null.

reasoning: A bound checks the argument’s type, not whether its contents resemble a number. Parsing text is a separate operation.

quizTarget: Add input.add(1) inside total. Why is the changed program rejected?

essentialSupport.fact: List<? extends Number> accepts a List<Integer> for reading as Number values. The ? stands for an unknown particular type. You cannot safely add an arbitrary non-null Number: the actual list might require Integer.

List<? super Integer> can receive Integer values; its actual element type is Integer or a supertype. Reading from that unknown list gives only Object without additional checks. The mnemonic is producer extends, consumer super.

List<Integer> is not a subtype of List<Number>. Wildcards express the particular flexibility an operation needs instead of pretending all lists accept the same additions. List.of creates an unmodifiable list; our output ArrayList is mutable.

reasoning: The compile-time wildcard restriction is enough to reject this addition, independently of whether a particular supplied list is mutable.

quizTarget: Change boxed to null while keeping the guard. What happens?

essentialSupport.fact: Autoboxing converts an int value to an Integer reference; unboxing retrieves the primitive int. Collections use reference types, so ArrayList<Integer> relies on these conversions when storing or retrieving ints.
An Integer reference can be null; int cannot. Unboxing null throws NullPointerException. A presence check must occur before the conversion, not after it.
== on two wrapper references tests identity, and caching can make results misleading. Use equals for non-null logical wrapper equality or compare deliberately unboxed primitives when safe.

reasoning: The reference is tested first. The declaration int value = boxed is reached only in the non-null branch.

quizTarget: Change the call to load(true). Which output follows?

essentialSupport.fact: An IOException is checked: code that may throw it must catch it or declare it with throws. RuntimeException subclasses such as IllegalArgumentException are unchecked and do not have that catch-or-declare requirement.

throw creates an abrupt exit toward a matching catch. In this demonstration no real file is read: load deliberately throws an IOException when fail is true. A thrown call supplies no normal return value.
catch(IOException error) handles that type, and getMessage reads its description. Do not catch every exception merely to pretend success; decide what recovery or propagation is appropriate.

reasoning: The normal print receives no value. The matching catch prints the message and execution then continues after the handler.

quizTarget: Call run(true) instead of run(false), taking the early return after body. What prints next?

essentialSupport.fact: try-with-resources manages AutoCloseable resources. It calls close when the try block exits, including a return or exception. This Trace only logs lifecycle events; real streams release external resources.
AutoCloseable declares close with a possible checked Exception, but Trace overrides it without throwing a checked exception. This example therefore needs no catch for close.

Multiple resources close in reverse initialization order. If the body throws and closing also throws, the body exception remains primary and close failures can be suppressed. Garbage collection is not a substitute for timely resource closure.

reasoning: Returning from run still exits its try block and closes the resource. The statement after the try is not reached.

quizTarget: Replace null with an empty String. Which branch runs?

essentialSupport.fact: Optional<String> holds a String or no value. Optional.ofNullable accepts a possibly null reference and produces an empty Optional for null. An empty string is still a present String.

isPresent tests presence; get requires a present value and otherwise throws NoSuchElementException. This explicit guard makes the example safe. Prefer APIs that clearly state whether absence is expected.

Optional.empty is not null and is not automatically an error. Do not use Optional itself as a null reference. Other combinators can transform values later; the present/absent distinction is the core here.

reasoning: Presence depends on whether a value exists, not whether the value has positive length. An empty String is a present value.

quizTarget: Pass null instead of "cat". What happens?

essentialSupport.fact: value instanceof String text checks whether value refers to a String and binds a String variable text when the test succeeds. It avoids a separate explicit cast after the test.
With &&, the right operand runs only when the left is true. text is therefore available in text.isEmpty() and in the successful if body. If value is null, this instanceof test is false.
This uses a reference-type pattern, a stable feature. No primitive patterns or preview flags are needed. Pattern matching does not turn unrelated object types into Strings.

reasoning: instanceof is false for null, so && skips the right side and the method reaches its fallback.

quizTarget: Supply new Excited() instead of new Plain(). What changes?

essentialSupport.fact: Composition means one object uses another object to perform part of its work. NoticeService has a Formatter; it is not a kind of Formatter. The constructor receives the collaborator explicitly.

Objects.requireNonNull checks the supplied reference and throws NullPointerException if absent. The final field prevents replacing that reference later, not every possible change inside the collaborator.
A second Formatter implementation can change formatting without subclassing NoticeService. This makes the dependency visible and allows small substitute implementations in tests.

reasoning: NoticeService delegates to the supplied Formatter object. The interface stays the same while the collaborator’s behavior changes.
